analysis: All four units are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md excerpts (lines 1414-2008, historical release notes) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md, with a date bump and a new section "Calibration ownership and foreground admission" plus one file-map row. No executable code, wire fields, key handling, attestation, encryption, or authorization behavior changes in the supplied text. The new doc section describes provider-local startup calibration: a single session per Mac, no change to activation or OS reserves, foreground customer requests cancel calibration and wait for actual retirement, and calibration observations are staged and published only after all requests retire and the posture check passes. It is documented as excluded from served-request and output-token totals, with capacity wire fields and the platform memory contract unchanged. Relevant threats are T-010 (cancellation propagation) and T-029 (idle GPU), plus T-041 and TB-007 for the allocator and cache. The doc says retirement releases request ownership but does not claim the allocator returns cached physical bytes to the OS. That caveat is consistent with T-028. The code files it references (IdleCalibrationCoordinator.swift, EngineV2Bridge+ModelCalibrationRequests.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Events.swift) were not supplied, so the claims, including that the foreground lease waits for retirement before admission, are unverified here. The next pass should check those source files if present in the PR for a calibration path that could delay customer admission without bound, or that could leak calibration prompts into the prefix cache (T-041). No changes to the threat model's assumptions are evident from this text.
